_README: ตัดสิน (Tatsin) — public routing config. The 7 `rooms` are the classes the shipped checkpoint was TRAINED on; their order maps to letters A-G, so do not reorder. The `label` string is the option TEXT the model scores — it is model-bound, not cosmetic: changing a label's wording without retraining degrades the pick. To route to your own classes, retrain (see README).
_rooms_note: channel_id is intentionally empty here. It exists only so a downstream consumer (a Discord bot, a ticket router) can map a picked room to its own destination. Put your own id in.

quarantine._note: Layer-3 destination. Deliberately NOT inside `rooms` (an 8th entry would shift the A-G letter map). The model never asks the user to confirm — it abstains and hands the item here.
quarantine.label: ห้องกัก (รอตรวจโดยคน)

identity._note: The wrapper answers the identity question itself; the classifier cannot emit a sentence. keywords are matched ONLY when the message IS the identity question (or has a polite lead-in) — never as a substring — because loose matching answered real work messages with the brand sentence and zero model calls.

pdpa._note: Mask PII BEFORE logging or sending to any model. Thai letters are word characters, so \b does not fire in unspaced Thai ('บัตรประชาชน1234567890123ครับ') and PII leaks — digit lookarounds are used instead.

gates._note_noul_bands: Calibrated on the project's Thai routing rows. Do NOT tighten without re-scoring — the pinning rows sit closer to the edge than the aggregate suggests.
gates._note_noul_sources: Only models that emit `noul` as a real probability belong here, and the entry is matched against the `source` field the endpoint puts on the wire (not a name we set). Models not listed fall back to the confidence gate. The value below is the source tag of THIS project's checkpoint (whose provenance — the open-source base engine it is fine-tuned from — is credited in NOTICE); replace it with your own checkpoint's source tag if you retrain.

nway._note: The small model was trained on pairwise A/B. `single` asks one 7-way question (off-distribution, cheap); `pairwise` seeds with one 7-way then runs an A/B knockout with position swapped (in-distribution, more calls). swap_check cancels the measured position bias. `max_calls` is the TOTAL per-request cap: the pairwise knockout needs 2 slots per pair (a pair is only trustworthy with its swap), and when a big model is configured one slot is reserved for the layer-2 escalation, so a request never exceeds max_calls calls end to end.

endpoints._note: Two connection points YOU set. (1) `tatsin_decide` = the small-model server (ships with this package, contract: POST {state, question, options[]} -> {pick, confidence, noul, margin, ranked, coverage, source}). (2) `big_openai` = the BIG-model API the ladder calls when the small model is NOT confident (layer 2). It is any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — a local Ollama/vLLM, or a hosted API. Leave it empty to turn layer 2 off (unsure -> quarantine); fill it to opt in. There is no house default.
endpoints._fallbacks: Env vars override the file. BIG (layer 2) is off when both TATSIN_BIG_URL and `big_openai` are empty: TATSIN_SMALL_URL / TATSIN_SMALL_NAME / TATSIN_BIG_URL / TATSIN_BIG_MODEL / TATSIN_BIG_KEY / TATSIN_API_KEY.
